For procurement teams · Ghana

Working with AfriScan in Ghana

What the Minerals Commission’s local procurement list, the Petroleum Commission permit, public procurement through GHANEPS, company registration with GIPA and the Data Protection Act 2012 mean when a mining company, a pipeline or power utility, a public body or a lender buys structure mapping, change records or drone work in Ghana, and what to ask any supplier for. A summary of public rules as of 27 September 2026, for orientation; it is not legal or tax advice.

Send tender documents How we work

In short

Five questions every supplier file in Ghana should answer

Who holds the contract?

On a mining lease, a Ghanaian firm that meets the ownership test wherever the local procurement list reserves the service. We treat our own mapping work as reserved under item 35 until counsel settles it. On upstream petroleum work, a company with a Petroleum Commission permit.

Which permits apply?

The Petroleum Commission permit for upstream work, and an environmental permit where the project itself is an undertaking listed in L.I. 2504.

Where is the supplier registered?

GHANEPS for government procurement, the PPA Supplier Portal, and company registration with GIPA, renewed every year.

Who flies the drone?

If the scope includes drone work, a company registered in Ghana whose GCAA ROC and Operations Specifications cover the job.

Who handles personal data?

Who is controller and who is processor, whether each is registered with the Data Protection Commission, and where imagery and results are processed and stored.

Mining local content

The Minerals Commission’s local procurement list

Mining procurement in Ghana follows L.I. 2431 and the Minerals Commission’s 6th-edition Local Procurement List, in force from 1 January 2025 and still the latest on the Commission’s local-content page on 27 September 2026. Among its items:

Item Service Condition
20 Security services Exclusive to Ghanaian firms
34 Civil works Exclusive to Ghanaian firms
35 “Geophysical Ground-based Survey; Mapping, Pitting and Trenching” “Strictly Incorporated in Ghana with Exclusive Ghanaian Directors and Shareholders”
36 “Geophysical Airborne-based Survey” Incorporated in Ghana, with at least 30 per cent Ghanaian directors and shareholders
43 Tailings Exclusive to Ghanaian firms

The Commission’s chief executive said in February 2026 that local content is to be “embedded in every mining agreement, procurement decision and employment policy” (Minerals Commission).

How we work on a mining lease

  • A qualifying Ghanaian firm holds the contract with the lease holder.
  • AfriScan is its technology supplier: imagery analysis, reviewed registers, GIS layers and reports.
  • The work is land and environmental mapping. It is never offered or described as security.
  • Any drone flight is flown by a company registered in Ghana whose ROC covers it.

Petroleum

The Petroleum Commission permit and local participation

Service companies working in upstream petroleum need a permit from the Petroleum Commission, set up under Act 821, “before commencement of operations”, and the permit is renewed every year (Petroleum Commission). The application asks for the certificate of incorporation and certificate to commence business, company regulations, tax, SSNIT and VAT certificates, a signed HSE policy, a business plan and company profile, financial statements, and certificates from professional bodies such as an “EPA Permit, Air Operator Certificate, NPA Licence, Aviation Licence”.

The Commission lists the petroleum local-content regulations, L.I. 2204 of 2013 as amended by L.I. 2435 of 2021, among its laws and regulations, with guidance that names joint ventures, channel partnerships and strategic alliances as routes for local participation. For an upstream contract, the proposal states which company holds the permit and how local participation is arranged.

Downstream petroleum is regulated by the National Petroleum Authority (Act 691), and electricity and natural-gas licensing by the Energy Commission, which also has local-content regulations for the power sector (L.I. 2354).

Public procurement

GHANEPS and the PPA Supplier Portal

Public bodies buy under the Public Procurement Act 2003 (Act 663), as amended by Act 914. The Ghana Electronic Procurement System, GHANEPS, is mandatory “for all government procurement” under a directive of 18 September 2023 and the notice of 23 November 2023, and suppliers register on it. The Public Procurement Authority also runs a Supplier Portal.

State utilities and agencies publish their own adverts and tenders as well. Tell us the portal, the tender reference and the prequalification category your process uses, and send any supplier forms with your request.

We respond to tenders, RFQs and requests for information; the proposal names the company that holds each registration your contract needs.

Company registration and drones

GIPA registration, and who may fly

The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Act, 2026 (Act 1173), assented to on 15 July 2026, replaced the GIPC Act 2013. According to the Authority’s notice, it removes the blanket minimum-capital requirements for wholly foreign-owned enterprises and joint ventures, keeps a reduced threshold for trading enterprises, and requires registered enterprises to renew their registration every year.

Commercial drone work needs a GCAA RPAS Operator Certificate, and only a company registered under the laws of Ghana can complete certification. For evaluation, split any scope into its satellite and desk-based part, which needs no aviation approval, and its drone part, which does. Afridrone is working towards the authorisations Ghana requires; every proposal with a drone element names the company that will fly it.

Drone rules in Ghana

Data protection

The Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843)

The Data Protection Commission says that “all entities involved in processing personal data are required to register” under s.27(1) of the Data Protection Act 2012, naming data controllers, data processors and “Foreign Companies – International businesses processing personal data within Ghana” (DPC registration). Processing while unregistered is barred (s.53) and is an offence (s.56). The application asks, among other things, for the countries to which personal data will be transferred and for the applicant’s security measures; renewal needs a compliance report, and the Commission’s guidance calls for a Data Protection Supervisor.

Aerial and satellite imagery of homes and compounds can contain personal data. The contract should say who is controller and who is processor, where imagery and results are processed and stored, which countries data goes to, and how long it is kept.

How we keep personal data down

  • Registers record structures and coordinates, not names.
  • We map land and assets, never people.
  • Results go only to the contacts you name.
  • The data terms for each project state where data is processed and stored, and for how long.

What we send

For your supplier file

  • A written proposal: scope, method, imagery plan, deliverables and schedule
  • The contracting arrangement: which company holds the contract, and why, where local-content rules apply
  • An imagery statement: sources, capture dates, licence terms and credits
  • For any drone element: the company that will fly it, with its GCAA ROC and Operations Specifications
  • The data terms: controller and processor, where data is processed and stored, and for how long
  • Sample outputs, and a redacted sample report on request

Tell us which registrations and certificates your process requires, and the reference of the tender or RFQ. The proposal answers each requirement in writing and names the company that holds each registration your contract needs.

Frequently asked questions

Does remote satellite mapping for a mine count as "Mapping" under the local procurement list?

Item 35 of the Minerals Commission’s list covers “Geophysical Ground-based Survey; Mapping, Pitting and Trenching (Strictly Incorporated in Ghana with Exclusive Ghanaian Directors and Shareholders)”. Whether it reaches remote satellite analysis delivered from outside Ghana has not been settled, and it is a question for counsel. Until it is, we treat work on a mining lease as falling under it and deliver through a qualifying Ghanaian firm.

Who holds the contract on a mining lease?

Because we treat work on a mining lease as falling under item 35 until counsel settles it, a firm incorporated in Ghana with exclusively Ghanaian directors and shareholders holds the contract with the lease holder. AfriScan supplies the imagery analysis, the reviewed registers and the GIS layers to that firm. If you already work with a qualifying Ghanaian survey or GIS firm, tell us in your request.

Which registrations do you hold in Ghana?

None yet. AfriScan does not hold any Ghanaian registration, permit or aviation approval today, and Afridrone is working towards the GCAA authorisations that drone work in Ghana needs. For each contract, the proposal names the company that holds each registration the contract needs, such as supplier registration on GHANEPS or the PPA Supplier Portal, a Petroleum Commission permit or Data Protection Commission registration, and, for any drone element, the Ghana-registered company whose GCAA ROC covers the flights. Ask for the evidence with the proposal.

Can you work under an upstream petroleum contract?

Service companies working for upstream operators need a Petroleum Commission permit before operations start. For an upstream contract, the proposal states which company holds the permit and contracts with you. The Commission’s local-content guidance lists joint ventures, channel partnerships and strategic alliances among the routes for local participation.

Where are imagery and results processed and stored?

The proposal and the data terms say so for your project, including any country outside Ghana to which data is transferred, because the Data Protection Commission’s registration asks for exactly that. Registers record structures and coordinates, not names.

Preparing a tender or a supplier file?

Send the tender or RFQ documents, the deadline and your supplier forms. The proposal answers each requirement and names the company that holds each registration your contract needs.
